paper_metadata.title: Implementing Quantum Machine Learning in Credit Card Fraud Detection

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical credit card fraud detection pipeline using amplitude-encoded transaction features processed by a variational quantum circuit and then classified by a classical neural network, evaluated on a public European credit card transaction dataset with a 70:30 train-test split on a quantum simulator.

algorithm.variant: VQC + classical neural network hybrid fraud classifier
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized quantum circuit with Hadamard, CNOT, and rotation gates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Transaction features (PCA-transformed V1-V30 plus Time and Amount) are normalized and encoded into quantum states; amplitude encoding uses log2(N) qubits for N features. Angle encoding is also discussed as an alternative, mapping each feature to a rotation angle on one qubit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize classification error / cost function C(θ) = <ψ_out|H|ψ_out> with H representing classification error.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Weighted loss function is used in the classical neural network to address class imbalance; no explicit quantum constraint-handling mechanism is reported.

problem_instance.description: Binary classification of credit card transactions as legitimate or fraudulent.
problem_instance.dataset_name: European Credit Card Transactions (Kaggle creditcardfraud dataset)

dataset_specification.description: September 2013 European credit card transactions; 284,807 total records; 492 fraudulent transactions (0.172%); 30 PCA-transformed features (V1-V30) plus Time and Amount; data split 70:30 for training/testing.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Imputation of missing values, standardization of numerical features, categorical variable encoding, PCA-transformed features retained as V1-V30, normalization before quantum encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single train-test evaluation on a 30% test split; metrics reported include precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Missing-value imputation, standardization, categorical encoding, PCA-based feature representation, normalization, and 70:30 train-test split.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: VQC measurement outputs are fed into a feedforward neural network; binary output thresholded at 0.5 to label transactions as legitimate or fraudulent.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states that QML may potentially outperform classical algorithms and could offer significant speedups as quantum hardware advances, but no empirical or asymptotic speedup is quantified.
